items.title: Renhuai123/ziwei-doushu
items.summary: Renhuai123/ziwei-doushu is an open-source TypeScript engine based on Ni Haixia's Tianji system that calculates Ziwei Doushu astrological charts. The project provides a large 13-dimensional astrological interpretation dataset (v4.0) covering dates between 1950 and 2026.

snapshot.description: 紫微斗数开源排盘引擎 — 基于倪海厦《天纪》体系，含完整排盘算法、四化系统、格局知识库、古籍原文数据. 1. 发布 13 维解读数据集 v4.0 —— 674,976 张命盘（公历 1950–2026 年每一个真实日期 × 12 时辰 × 男女）× 13 维 = 8,774,688 段解读，正文约 204 亿字。解压后 56.6 GB（v3.0 为 33.1 GB，增加 71%），压缩后只有 161 MB，按年份分 77 个文件，可以只下需要的年份，也可以一次下全年份总包。下载见 Release v4.0-13d，规格和字段见第二·新章。发布前 77 个文件逐个解压，与原始数据逐字节比对一致。

items.title: SnailSploit/Claude-Red
items.summary: SnailSploit/Claude-Red is an offensive security skills library prepared for the Claude AI capability system. It provides expert methodologies for various attack surfaces, such as SQL injection and shellcode development, through structured files.

snapshot.description: claude-red is a curated library of offensive security skills designed for the Claude skills system. Each skill is a structured SKILL.md file that primes Claude with expert-level methodology for a specific attack surface — from SQLi to shellcode, EDR evasion to exploit development.

items.title: OpenBMB/VoxCPM
items.summary: Developed by OpenBMB, VoxCPM produces continuous speech representations directly in text-to-speech (TTS) processes thanks to its tokenizer-free structure. With its end-to-end diffusion autoregressive architecture, it offers multilingual speech generation, creative sound design, and realistic voice cloning capabilities.

snapshot.description: VoxCPM2: Tokenizer-Free TTS for Multilingual Speech Generation, Creative Voice Design, and True-to-Life Cloning. VoxCPM is a tokenizer-free Text-to-Speech system that directly generates continuous speech representations via an end-to-end diffusion autoregressive architecture, bypassing discrete tokenization to achieve highly natural and expressive synthesis.

items.title: nodejs/node
items.summary: Node.js is an open-source (source code accessible to everyone) runtime environment that allows JavaScript code to be executed outside the browser. This infrastructure, which can run on different operating systems, is widely preferred for server-side application development.

snapshot.description: Node.js JavaScript runtime ✨🐢🚀✨. Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime environment.

items.title: Local Wikipedia: Wikipedia, but only for things a half hour walk from you
items.summary: Local Wikipedia is an encyclopedia project that provides information about places within a half-hour walking distance of the user's current location. Aiming to increase environmental awareness, this platform scales general Wikipedia content down to a local level.

snapshot.description: Wikipedia, but only for things a half hour walk from you.

items.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro and K3.1 Pro Highspeed
items.summary: Kimi K3.1 Pro and Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed are among generative AI models. These models offer up-to-date options designed for users to perform complex tasks.

items.title: Today, we hacked what we'd set out to hack: the iPhone
items.summary: Security researchers announced that they have successfully completed a hack they aimed to perform on an iPhone. This study refers to a technical process conducted regarding the smartphone's security vulnerabilities.

snapshot.description: Today, we hacked what we'd set out to hack: the iPhone.

items.title: Apple Music 404 Not Found
items.summary: A hidden error page has been discovered on the website of the Apple Music digital music platform. The 404 page in question presents a different design for links that users cannot access.

items.title: Canadians are running out of time to oppose Bill C-22
items.summary: The bill codenamed Bill C-22, currently being discussed in the Canadian Parliament, has the potential to threaten the privacy and security rights of millions by expanding surveillance powers. There is limited time left for public reaction against the lawful access regulation, which has passed the House of Commons and is currently on the agenda of the Canadian Senate.

items.title: TARSphere: A Robot-Oriented Full-Stack Framework for Long-Horizon Embodied Agents in Evolving Physical and Social Environments
items.summary: TARSphere is a full-stack framework developed for robotic agents moving under physical and social constraints. Operating on a physics simulator, the system aims for robots to adapt to changing environmental conditions and human needs with long-term goals.

snapshot.description: Robots must act under physical and social constraints while adapting to changes in their environment and human needs. Existing embodied-agent systems often focus on specified goals or abstract execution into symbolic actions, limiting evaluation in an evolving world. We introduce TARSphere, a robot-oriented full-stack framework for physically and socially grounded long-horizon embodied agents. TARSphere-Infra runs robot policies in a physics simulator with embodied NPCs and constrained dialogue.

items.title: The LLM-Attacker: A Unified Red-Team Framework for Privacy Evaluation of Split and Distributed LLM Systems
items.summary: The LLM-Attacker provides a unified red-team framework for the privacy assessment of split and distributed large language model (LLM) systems. It aims to standardize data recovery processes by allowing researchers to record, compare, and extend different attack methods.

snapshot.description: Split language models keep input text on a client but send intermediate representations to a server. Attacks can reconstruct text from these messages. Comparing privacy evaluations is difficult when attackers see different messages, know different model weights or use different datasets and recovery measures. items.title: EvalResearchBench: Can AI Agents Build Their Own Feedback for Recursive Self-Improvement?
items.summary: EvalResearchBench is a benchmark tool that investigates whether artificial intelligence agents can autonomously design the evaluation mechanisms they need for recursive self-improvement processes. This study aims to automate evaluation processes using software interfaces (APIs) to reduce the cost of complex tests.

snapshot.description: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) relies on evaluation feedback to assess progress and guide further research, yet repeatedly running complex benchmarks is costly and slows iteration. Human experts reduce this cost by selecting benchmark subsets or designing compact suites. We ask whether AI agents can automate this design process and introduce EvalResearchBench (ERB), a benchmark for autonomous evaluation research. items.title: Diffusion Language Models Change Speed Across Tasks and Languages
items.summary: Diffusion language models generate multiple tokens in a single forward pass, dynamically determining the number of steps in the generation process based on the tasks. Research shows that tasks where input text is copied or edited are lower cost, while free-text generation is higher cost.

snapshot.description: Diffusion language models can write several tokens in one forward pass, and they decide during generation how many passes to spend. Two outputs of the same token length can therefore vary a lot in cost. To understand the underlying factors of this cost variation, we analyze two diffusion models across 10 tasks. items.title: Different Tasks, Different Timesteps: Temporal Task-Aware Quantization for Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: T 2Quant, developed for Diffusion Language Models (DLMs), reveals that quantization precision in the iterative denoising process varies according to task and time variables. This method offers a mixed-precision quantization strategy by predicting the precision requirements needed by different tasks without requiring label data.

snapshot.description: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) introduce unique quantization challenges due to their iterative denoising process. In this work, we reveal that quantization sensitivity is both taskand time-dependent, with different downstream tasks exhibiting distinct precision requirements across denoising steps. We further show that these patterns can be predicted without groundtruth labels or task-specific evaluation metrics.
